whatsABoundarySurvey.headline: What is a boundary survey?
whatsABoundarySurvey.description: A boundary survey determines the legal property lines of a parcel of land. Using advanced GPS, total stations, and historical land records, SmartGrid Surveying provides highly accurate maps that define property limits and identify any encroachments or discrepancies.

postHeroCta.description: Registry-accurate boundary surveys prepared by licensed surveyors and packaged for Ardhisasa submission — for buyers, landowners and developers.

process.headline: Boundary Survey Process — From Site Visit to County Approval
process.description: A transparent, six-step cadastral workflow. You always know which stage your parcel is in and exactly what happens next.

steps.label: Site Visit & Document Review
steps.description: We walk the parcel with you, review the title deed, deed plan and prior surveys, and record existing occupation and improvements.

steps.label: Registry (Ardhisasa / RIM) Verification
steps.description: Parcel records are retrieved and cross-checked against the Registry Index Map (RIM) and the Ardhisasa cadastral database to confirm the legal boundaries.

steps.label: GNSS Field Survey (RTK Control)
steps.description: RTK GNSS and total station observations establish a control network tied to the national grid for centimetre-level accuracy.

steps.label: Beaconing & Boundary Confirmation
steps.description: Boundary corners are computed, confirmed with adjoining owners, and permanent beacons are placed or re-fixed on the ground.

steps.label: Plan Preparation & Computation
steps.description: Observations are reduced and adjusted; areas, traverses and final survey plans are computed and checked by a licensed surveyor.

steps.label: Submission & County Approval
steps.description: The compiled cadastral documentation is lodged with the registry (Ardhisasa) and county offices for approval and registration.

compliance.headline: Legal & Ardhisasa Compliance You Can Rely On
compliance.description: Every cadastral survey we deliver is executed under the statutes that govern land in Kenya — so your documents survive scrutiny at the registry, the bank and the court.

checklist.title: Land Registration Act, 2012
checklist.description: Surveys prepared for registration under the Act governing title deeds, parcel boundaries and transfers in Kenya.

checklist.title: Survey Act, Cap 299
checklist.description: All fieldwork, computations and plans conform to the Survey Act and its Regulations — signed by a licensed surveyor.

checklist.title: Ardhisasa Cadastral Submission Requirements
checklist.description: Deliverables are packaged to Ardhisasa digital lodgement standards: georeferenced data, deed plans and supporting documents.

checklist.title: County Approval Process
checklist.description: We liaise with county planning offices for subdivision consents and development approvals tied to your survey.

checklist.title: ISK Compliance & Licensed Surveyor
checklist.description: Work is executed and signed off by an Institution of Surveyors of Kenya (ISK) registered, licensed surveyor.

caseStudy.headline: Kiambu Subdivision Survey – 40-Acre Parcel
caseStudy.subtitle: Title Registration & Boundary Dispute Resolution Using High-Precision GNSS Surveying

overview.label: 01 · Project Overview
paragraphs: A 40-acre parcel in Kiambu County required formal subdivision, cadastral verification, and resolution of long-standing boundary disputes between adjoining landowners.
critical: Title deed processing under Kenyan land registry requirements
Enabling future development and land sales
overview.deployNote: SmartGrid Surveying deployed RTK GNSS, total station control networks, and registry reconciliation workflows to restore spatial accuracy and legal clarity.

challenge.label: 02 · The Challenge (Before Condition)
items: Overlapping parcel claims in adjacent subdivisions
Lack of georeferenced control tied to modern coordinate systems

images.alt: Disturbed boundary beacon awaiting re-establishment on site
Adjoining parcels with overlapping claims in Kiambu County
Overgrown and unmarked boundary line on the Kiambu parcel before the survey

methodology.label: 03 · Survey Methodology & GPS Workflow
methodology.intro: A structured engineering-grade workflow was applied to ensure legal and spatial accuracy in compliance with Kenyan cadastral standards and Ardhisasa requirements.

steps.title: Step 1: Desk Study & Registry Retrieval
points: Reviewed historical deed plans and parcel references

steps.title: Step 2: Establishment of Control Network
points: RTK GNSS base station setup on stable benchmark
Primary control points established across parcel corners
Total station used for dense control in obstructed zones

steps.title: Step 3: Field Boundary Reconstruction
points: Walked perimeter with landowners and witnesses
Identified existing beacons and restored missing markers

steps.title: Step 4: Data Processing & Adjustment
points: Coordinate transformation into UTM Arc 1960 system
Least squares adjustment of control network

steps.title: Step 5: Subdivision Design & Legal Drafting
points: Parcel segmentation based on agreed ownership units
Preparation for submission to land registry

images.alt: RTK GNSS receiver set up over a control point on the parcel
Surveyor confirming a restored boundary beacon in the field

outcome.label: 04 · Outcome (After Condition)
outcome.intro: The intervention resulted in a fully resolved cadastral structure with legal and spatial clarity.
deliverables: Accurate subdivision plan approved for registration

items.text: Enabled formal title processing for all subdivided units
Increased land valuation potential due to legal clarity
Provided a permanent geospatial reference dataset for future developments
Reduced risk exposure for buyers and developers

rows.specification: Kenyan Land Act + Survey Act Cap 299

engineeringNote.label: 07 · Final Engineering Note
engineeringNote.text: This project demonstrates how modern GNSS-based cadastral surveying eliminates ambiguity in land ownership boundaries while ensuring compliance with Kenyan land registration frameworks. SmartGrid Surveying integrates field precision + legal geospatial intelligence to convert disputed land into registrable, investment-ready assets.
